description: The substance registry's public mirror (galaxy plan 14, P14.T49.a and P14.T54.a; decision-composition 1.1; decision-p14-t54a-grain-density 2): each row in index order, append-only, with its key, kind, molar mass (g/mol), heat_capacity_over_r_298k (a gas row's ideal-gas c_p/R at 298.15 K, the sum over its molecular constants, for display and cross-check only; null for a row with no gas columns), the client optics the sim may ask of it, and its grain density without pore space. grain_density_variant names the index-file variant whose composition the densities are (null: the substance itself). solid_grain_density and liquid_grain_density are each null, where none was read at any temperature, or pieces of nodes: temperatures_k (K) strictly rising, densities_kg_per_m3 (kg/m3) finite and positive, the two of equal length, at least one. To evaluate a phase's density at T: if its member is null there is none; otherwise take the piece with from_k <= T < to_k, the member's last piece also covering T = to_k and a null bound being unbounded, and if no piece covers T there is none; within the piece the density is the first node's at or below it, the last node's above it, and between the nodes T0 < T <= T1 it is rho0 + f (rho1 - rho0) with f = (T - T0) / (T1 - T0). It holds the sim's Substance::grain_density within 1e-4 (relative) wherever both give one, each node to the bit. A row with a phase diagram gives each solid phase's density with a piece of its own, a phase with none being a gap (a last piece that ends where one begins ends at the double below its start, so that the start reads none), and its saturated liquid from the triple temperature to 0.99 of the critical temperature only: the sim gives one above it too, to the critical density, which no linear table follows. Any other row holds each phase that was read at its stated temperature, one node held at every temperature. Written by crates/hyperion-sim/tests/substance_golden.rs under HYPERION_BLESS=1 and checked against the registry otherwise; never edit it by hand.
